Reproducing Mu et al. (2019) from dandiset 000350¶

Paper. Mu Y, Bennett DV, Rubinov M, Narayan S, Yang C-T, Tanimoto M, Mensh BD, Looger LL, Ahrens MB (2019). Glia accumulate evidence that actions are futile and suppress unsuccessful behavior. Cell 178, 27-43. doi:10.1016/j.cell.2019.05.050. The paper is open access (CC BY-NC-ND). This attempt used its full text (main text and STAR Methods); the Supplemental Information was not read.

Dandiset. DANDI:000350, version 0.240822.1759. The paper cites no dandiset version (it predates the dandiset). Two versions are published, 0.221219.1506 and 0.240822.1759. The later one is pinned: it is the most recent, and it corrects the imaging plane of the three files with radial astrocytes only, which the earlier version names NeuronVolume ("for the neuron filter"). The data the analysis uses (swim bouts, cell traces) are the same in both; the data check shows this.

What the dandiset holds. 12 light-sheet sessions of paralysed larval zebrafish swimming fictively in virtual reality, each with the swim and stimulus signals of the rig, the detected swim bouts and a table of behavioural states. Eight files also hold segmented cell traces: 4 of neurons and radial astrocytes imaged together, 4 of neurons only. The other 4 hold raw images only. None of the perturbation experiments of Figures 4 to 7 is in it.

Code. The paper links its cell segmentation code, https://github.com/mikarubi/segmentation (now voluseg), read at commit 54d1907b1d911ad6445428f8a79ca44875ed42b1 (27 June 2019, the last before publication). It holds motion correction, brain masking, cell detection, baseline estimation and the first NMF of cell traces (z6_components.py), with censor_tau = [30, 30] and baseline_tau = 300 s. It holds no behavioural analysis, no passivity detection, no clustering of components across fish and no onset analysis, so every choice below on those comes from the Methods or is made here and stated.

This is the second version of the notebook. After the first verification round it adds the protocol-code check, a variant that keeps the epochs cut by the edges of a condition period, the closed-loop passivity by gain level before and after the first open loop, the SD within periods, the first onsets after each switch and a stretch of the raw traces in two fish, and it limits the bouts counted after a switch to open loop to that open-loop period (fig1c). After the second round it adds the passivity onsets of the two-colour fish by protocol code and the SD within 10 s windows (figs2a), and corrects text the outputs did not support.

import os
os.environ.setdefault("OMP_NUM_THREADS", "1")
import time
import warnings

import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import numpy as np
import pandas as pd
from scipy import stats

import fictive as fv

pd.set_option("display.width", 220)
pd.set_option("display.max_columns", 40)
pd.set_option("display.max_rows", 200)
warnings.filterwarnings("ignore", category=RuntimeWarning)

started = time.time()
sessions = fv.load_all()
S = {s["fish"]: s for s in sessions}
print(f"loaded {len(sessions)} files from dandiset {fv.DANDISET_ID} version {fv.DANDISET_VERSION} "
      f"in {time.time() - started:.0f} s")

# Whole-brain signal: mean DfOverF over an evenly spaced subset of ROI blocks, for every processed
# series; and, for one fish, a disjoint subset to check that the subset does not matter.
t0 = time.time()
jobs = [(s, name, 0.0) for s in sessions for name in s["imaging"]]
jobs += [(S["20170113-4"], "NeuronDfOverF", 0.5), (S["20170228-4"], "GliaDfOverF", 0.5)]
WB = fv.whole_brain_means(jobs)
print(f"whole-brain signals of {len(WB)} series in {time.time() - t0:.0f} s")

The files hold 12 fish aged 6 to 8 days, as in the Methods (5 to 7 dpf for behaviour, one at P8D). The Methods (Figure 2D and 2E) used 5 fish with neuronal GCaMP6f and 6 with glial GCaMP6f in separate lines. Here the neuron-only GCaMP6f files are 5 (4 with traces, 1 with raw images only), and the glia-only GCaMP6f files are 3, all with raw images only. The 4 two-colour files label both planes GCaMP6f, but their glial plane is excited at 561 nm and detected at 660 nm, which is the jRGECO1b channel of the Methods (Tg(gfap:jRGECO1b); Tg(elavl3:GCaMP6f), the line of Figure 2B and 2C). The data disagree with the indicator stated for the glial plane of these files. The raw series are stored as TwoPhotonSeries and the archive lists "two-photon microscopy technique", while the Methods describe a one-photon light-sheet microscope.

Stated units: {'SwimSignals': 'a.u.', 'StimulusGainSignal': 'a.u.'}

No two files share bout times or length, so each recording is counted once. Swim bout width equals stop minus start (in seconds), though the table describes it as "Estimated width spanned by the swim event". Swim power and the stimulus signals are in arbitrary units, as stated. In two files (20170203-1 and 20170228-4) some bouts have a power of exactly 0. The gain signal takes values from 0 to 0.036 (arbitrary units; the Methods give none for the gain), and the grating's baseline velocity takes 0, 0.5, 1, 1.5 or 2 (arbitrary units, against 2.86 mm/s in the Methods). The first column of StimulusParameterSignals holds protocol codes (12, 22, 23, 32, 33, 51, 52, 53); no file describes them, and the analysis uses the gain and velocity signals instead. What the codes hold is checked below.

# Protocol codes: what each undocumented code of StimulusParameterSignals (first column) holds.
rows = []
for s in sessions:
    c, t = s["protocol_code"].astype(int), s["cond_t"]
    edges = np.r_[0, np.flatnonzero(np.diff(c)) + 1, len(c)]
    for code_ in np.unique(c):
        m = c == code_
        blocks = [t[min(j, len(t) - 1)] - t[i] for i, j in zip(edges[:-1], edges[1:]) if c[i] == code_]
        g = np.round(s["gain"][m], 3)
        rows.append({"fish": s["fish"], "code": code_, "seconds": round(m.sum() / fv.COND_HZ), "blocks": len(blocks),
                     "median_block_s": round(float(np.median(blocks)), 1), "first_s": round(t[m][0]), "last_s": round(t[m][-1]),
                     "gain_levels": len(np.unique(g)), "gain_min": g.min(), "gain_max": g.max(),
                     "velocities": sorted(set(np.round(s["velocity"][m], 2)))})
codes = pd.DataFrame(rows)
print(codes.to_string(index=False))

# Code 33: the baseline velocity just before, during and just after each block.
rows = []
for s in sessions:
    c, v = s["protocol_code"].astype(int), s["velocity"]
    starts = np.flatnonzero((c[1:] == 33) & (c[:-1] != 33)) + 1
    for i in starts:
        j = i + np.argmax(c[i:] != 33)
        rows.append({"fish": s["fish"], "before": v[i - 2], "during": v[i], "after": v[j + 1], "dur_s": (j - i) / fv.COND_HZ,
                     "gain_during": s["gain"][i]})
c33 = pd.DataFrame(rows)
print(f"\nCode 33 blocks: {len(c33)} in {c33.fish.nunique()} files; duration {c33.dur_s.min():.1f} to {c33.dur_s.max():.1f} s; "
      f"gain during {c33.gain_during.max():.3f} at most; velocity during above before in {(c33.during > c33.before).sum()}, "
      f"equal in {(c33.during == c33.before).sum()}, below in {(c33.during < c33.before).sum()}, zero during in {(c33.during == 0).sum()}")

# TotalStimulusVelocitySignal, described as "(drift speed - motosensory gain) x swim power".
rows = []
for s in sessions:
    tv = s["total_velocity"]
    rows.append({"fish": s["fish"], "total_velocity_min": tv.min(), "total_velocity_max": tv.max(),
                 "baseline_velocity_max": s["velocity"].max(),
                 "corr_with_baseline_velocity": np.corrcoef(tv, s["velocity"][:len(tv)])[0, 1]})
print("\n", pd.DataFrame(rows).round(4).to_string(index=False))

# One session of each kind of protocol: gain, baseline velocity and code over time.
show = ["20161022-1", "20170113-4", "20170228-3", "20170228-4"]
fig, axes = plt.subplots(len(show), 1, figsize=(11, 2.2 * len(show)), sharex=False)
for ax, f in zip(axes, show):
    s = S[f]
    ax.plot(s["cond_t"], s["gain"] / max(s["gain"].max(), 1e-9), lw=0.6, label="gain (scaled to its max)")
    ax.plot(s["cond_t"], s["velocity"] / s["velocity"].max(), lw=0.6, label="baseline velocity (scaled)")
    ax2 = ax.twinx(); ax2.plot(s["cond_t"], s["protocol_code"], color="k", lw=0.6); ax2.set_ylabel("code")
    ax.set_title(f"{f}: gain max {s['gain'].max():.3f}, velocity max {s['velocity'].max():.1f}, codes {sorted(set(s['protocol_code'].astype(int)))}", fontsize=8)
    ax.set_ylim(-0.05, 1.05)
axes[0].legend(fontsize=7, loc="lower right"); axes[-1].set_xlabel("time (s)")
plt.tight_layout(); plt.show()

# Switches from closed to open loop in the two-colour files, with the open period's length and bouts.
rows = []
for s in sessions:
    if "GliaDfOverF" not in s["imaging"]:
        continue
    m, t = fv.condition_masks(s), s["cond_t"]
    segs = fv.segments(t, m["open"], 0)
    for t0 in t[1:][m["closed"][:-1] & m["open"][1:]]:
        end = min((b for a, b in segs if abs(a - t0) < 0.2), default=np.nan)
        rows.append({"fish": s["fish"], "switch_s": t0, "open_s": end - t0,
                     "bouts": int(((s["swims"].start_time >= t0) & (s["swims"].start_time < end)).sum())})
sw2 = pd.DataFrame(rows)
print("\nClosed-to-open switches in the two-colour files:")
print(sw2.groupby("fish").agg(switches=("switch_s", "size"), open_s_min=("open_s", "min"), open_s_max=("open_s", "max"),
                              bouts_min=("bouts", "min"), bouts_max=("bouts", "max"),
                              switches_with_16_bouts=("bouts", lambda b: int((b >= 16).sum()))).round(1).to_string())

The protocol codes are not described in any file; what they hold, from the signals:

  • 22 and 23 alternate in blocks with median lengths of 2 to 24 s, with the gain above 0 and the grating moving or stationary (closed loop, with stationary periods). In 20161109-2 these blocks also run with the gain at 0, so its short open-loop periods follow stationary grating, not closed loop.
  • 32 is prolonged open loop, in blocks of 35 to 41 s (medians) separated by code 33. Code 33 lasts 0.3 to 0.5 s with the gain at 0; the grating moves faster during it than before it in 390 of the 462 blocks and at the same speed in 72, and it is never stationary. It is a brief speed-up of the grating, not the static then forward stimulus of Figure 1K, and nothing says what it is for.
  • 51 and 53 alternate in blocks with median lengths of 12 to 125 s. In six files 51 has the gain above 0 and 53 has it at 0 (alternating closed and open loop), but in 20170228-4 both have the gain at 0, and in 20170228-3 code 51 has the gain at 0 for part of the time, so the two codes cannot be read as closed and open loop there.
  • 52 appears in 20170113-4 and 20170127-1, with 16 and 22 gain levels (from 0 and from 0.009), consistent with a randomised gain such as that of Figure 7C.
  • 12 appears once, for 3.4 s in 20170228-3.

TotalStimulusVelocitySignal is described as the drift speed minus the gain, times the swim power, but its values lie between -0.002 and 0.008 in every file, against baseline velocities of 0.5 to 2, so it is not that velocity. The visual feedback each bout produced, and so a replayed stimulus or a per-bout feedback probability, cannot be recovered from the files; only the baseline velocity and the gain are usable. Among the two-colour files, only 20170203-1 has more than 4 switches from closed to open loop (18; 7 of them followed by 16 or more bouts in the open-loop period). In 20170228-3 and 20170228-4, 2 of 4 and 3 of 3 switches are followed by 16 or more bouts, and the 3 open-loop periods of 20170228-4 hold 570 to 1218 bouts each.

The ActivityStates table is described only as "Classified periods of activity (passive, active, or transient)". In the three glia-only files it holds 3 rows; in the others it starts at or after the first open loop, and in sessions that later alternate closed and open loop it runs through both without saying which. Its "transient" rows are not defined in the paper, and in the files with more than 3 rows all of them, or all but one, are also listed with the same times as active rows. Many active rows last 5 s or less, which the Methods' definition of an active epoch excludes. The table is therefore not the Methods' classification as written; the claims use epochs built from the swim bouts by the Methods' rule, and the table as a variant.

NeuronDfOverF (first 200 ROIs, stored as float64, unit a.u.): DfOverF median 0.9930, range 0.728 to 2.833, per-ROI mean 1.0000 to 1.0000

  Fluorescence median -0.0100, range -0.167 to 0.001; median absolute change between frames 0.00e+00 (DfOverF 4.05e-03)
  • The imaging timestamps equal the rising edges of the camera trigger (FrameCaptureTTLSignal above 3.8), so imaging and behaviour share the rig's clock. In 20170113-2 the trigger has 9751 volume starts but the imaging series only 7616: the last 2135 volumes are not in the file.
  • The volume rate is 1.6 to 2.9 Hz, against "3 volumes/second" in the Methods; the two-colour sessions are the slowest.
  • In 20170113-4 the raw image series holds 3065 volumes, starting at 3292 s, while the traces cover 12050 volumes from the start; in 20170228-4 the raw series holds 5776 volumes against 7200 traces. Raw images are missing for part of these sessions.
  • The series called DfOverF is not a ΔF/F as the Methods define it (baseline-subtracted and divided by the baseline, so near 0 at rest). In the single-colour files it is each ROI's trace divided by its mean (every ROI mean is 1, float64); in the two-colour files it is centred near 0 (float32) with its first 60 s held constant, as the code's censoring (censor_tau) does. The two groups were processed differently. The Fluorescence series changes by about 2e-6 per frame in the single-colour file and not at all from frame to frame in the median ROI of the two-colour file, which is consistent with a slowly varying baseline, not raw fluorescence; its description is the same as that of DfOverF. The analysis therefore compares the whole-brain signal only within a fish, against a baseline window or between conditions, and drops the censored frames.

# Does the ROI subset matter? Correlate the whole-brain signal from two disjoint subsets.
for fish, name in [("20170113-4", "NeuronDfOverF"), ("20170228-4", "GliaDfOverF")]:
    a, na = WB[(fish, name, 0.0)]
    b, nb = WB[(fish, name, 0.5)]
    ok = ~fv.censored(a)
    print(f"{fish} {name}: subsets of {na} and {nb} ROIs, correlation {np.corrcoef(a[ok], b[ok])[0, 1]:.3f}")

# Clock check: whole-brain neuronal signal against the swim rate, with the true bout times and
# with the bouts shifted by 60 to 600 s (circularly), for every file with neuronal traces.
rng = np.random.default_rng(0)
rows = []
for s in sessions:
    if "NeuronDfOverF" not in s["imaging"]:
        continue
    t = s["imaging"]["NeuronDfOverF"]["t"]
    y = WB[(s["fish"], "NeuronDfOverF", 0.0)][0]
    ok = ~fv.censored(y)
    t, y = t[ok], y[ok]
    rate = fv.swim_rate(s, t)
    dt = np.median(np.diff(t))
    lags = np.arange(-int(10 / dt), int(10 / dt) + 1)
    def best(r):
        cc = [np.corrcoef(r[max(0, -l):len(r) - max(0, l)], y[max(0, l):len(y) - max(0, -l)])[0, 1] for l in lags]
        return np.max(cc), lags[np.argmax(cc)] * dt
    true_cc, true_lag = best(rate)
    null = [best(np.roll(rate, int(sh / dt)))[0] for sh in rng.uniform(60, 600, 20) * rng.choice([-1, 1], 20)]
    rows.append({"fish": s["fish"], "peak_corr": true_cc, "peak_lag_s": true_lag,
                 "shifted_max": np.max(null), "shifted_median": np.median(null)})
clock = pd.DataFrame(rows)
print("\nNeuronal whole-brain signal against swim rate (positive lag: signal after swims):")
print(clock.round(3).to_string(index=False))
print("Files where the true peak correlation exceeds every shifted one:", int((clock.peak_corr > clock.shifted_max).sum()), "of", len(clock))

The whole-brain signal from two disjoint ROI subsets is nearly the same, so the subset stands for the whole brain. In every file with neuronal traces, the neuronal signal follows swimming more closely with the true bout times than with any of 20 shifted copies, with its peak 0.3 to 5 s after the swims, which is consistent with the stated shared clock. The four raw-only files are used for behaviour only, which is on the rig's clock by construction.

Epochs used by the claims¶

Passive and active epochs are built from the swim bouts by the Methods' rule (see fictive.py), within each closed- or open-loop period; epochs cut by a period's edge are left out, as the claims file fixes. This drops the chain of bouts that runs into a switch to open loop, and with it the first passivity onset of an open-loop period when the fish swims across the switch. A variant keeps these epochs (keep_edges); the synthetic check below shows the difference, and the table gives the onsets each fish loses under the main rule.

    rows.append({"fish": f, **{f"{c}_{k}": sum(len(x[k]) for x in e[c]) for c in ["closed", "open"] for k in ["passive", "active"]},
                 "passivity_onsets": len(ON[f])})
print(pd.DataFrame(rows).to_string(index=False))

Result: partially reproduced. Under reading (a), epochs built from the swim bouts in open loop, passive epochs last 20.47 s on average over the 12 fish (within 24.4 +/- 4.9) and active epochs hold 19.06 bouts (within 29 +/- 11.8), but active epochs last 22.36 s, outside 36.1 +/- 8.2. Readings (b), the ActivityStates table (18.19 and 15.77 s), and (c), pooled epochs (18.81 s, 19.66 s, 15.99 bouts), put none of the values within tolerance. Fish differ widely (active epochs 7.3 to 64.1 s). With a pause threshold of 6 s the means are 21.46 and 25.31 s. Keeping the epochs cut by the edges of an open-loop period (a variant) gives 20.87 s, 21.20 s and 18.06 bouts, again 2 of 3 within tolerance, so leaving them out does not explain the short active epochs.

methods-isi¶

In closed loop fish swim in discrete bouts about once per second (inter-swim interval 1.2 +/- 0.05 s, n = 74), and within active epochs of open loop the interval is 1.19 +/- 0.047 s.

Readings: (a) start to start, (b) end to start; in closed loop (i) intervals under 5 s, (ii) all. Tolerances 1.96 SEM: 1.2 +/- 0.098 s and 1.19 +/- 0.092 s.

In [12]:
rows = []
for s in sessions:
    f = s["fish"]
    r = {"fish": f}
    for c in ["closed"]:
        ss, ee = [], []
        for seg in fv.segments(s["cond_t"], fv.condition_masks(s)[c]):
            w = s["swims"][(s["swims"].start_time >= seg[0]) & (s["swims"].stop_time <= seg[1])].sort_values("start_time")
            ss += list(np.diff(w.start_time.to_numpy()))
            ee += list(w.start_time.to_numpy()[1:] - w.stop_time.to_numpy()[:-1])
        ss, ee = np.array(ss), np.array(ee)
        r.update({"closed_a_i": ss[ee < 5].mean(), "closed_a_ii": ss.mean(), "closed_b_i": ee[ee < 5].mean(), "closed_b_ii": ee.mean(),
                  "closed_n": len(ss)})
    act = [e for x in EP[f]["open"] for e in x["active"]]
    r["active_a"] = np.mean(np.concatenate([np.diff(e["bout_starts"]) for e in act]))
    sw = s["swims"].set_index("start_time")
    gaps = []
    for e in act:
        b = s["swims"][(s["swims"].start_time >= e["start"]) & (s["swims"].stop_time <= e["stop"])].sort_values("start_time")
        gaps += list(b.start_time.to_numpy()[1:] - b.stop_time.to_numpy()[:-1])
    r["active_b"] = np.mean(gaps)
    rows.append(r)
isi = pd.DataFrame(rows)
print(isi.round(3).to_string(index=False))
print()
for cl, op in [("closed_a_i", "active_a"), ("closed_a_ii", "active_a"), ("closed_b_i", "active_b"), ("closed_b_ii", "active_b")]:
    c, o = isi[cl].mean(), isi[op].mean()
    ok_c, ok_o = abs(c - 1.2) <= 0.098, abs(o - 1.19) <= 0.092
    print(f"{cl} / {op}: closed loop {c:.3f} s ({'within' if ok_c else 'outside'} 1.2 +/- 0.098), "
          f"active epochs {o:.3f} s ({'within' if ok_o else 'outside'} 1.19 +/- 0.092); SEM {isi[cl].sem():.3f} and {isi[op].sem():.3f}")
print(f"\nRange over fish, closed_a_i {isi.closed_a_i.min():.2f} to {isi.closed_a_i.max():.2f} s; active_a {isi.active_a.min():.2f} to {isi.active_a.max():.2f} s")

fig1j-open-loop-passivity¶

Fish spend much more time in the passive state when swimming produces no visual feedback (open loop) than in closed loop with a naturalistic gain, where passivity is rare.

Criterion: fraction of time in pauses of 5 s or more, open against closed loop, one-sided Wilcoxon over fish at p < 0.05, and median closed-loop fraction below 10%.

In [13]:
rows = []
for s in sessions:
    f = s["fish"]
    r = {"fish": f}
    for c in ["closed", "open"]:
        tot = sum(x["seg"][1] - x["seg"][0] for x in EP[f][c])
        r[f"{c}_s"] = tot
        r[f"{c}_passive_frac"] = sum(b - a for x in EP[f][c] for a, b in x["pauses"]) / tot
    # Variant: closed loop before the first open loop only.
    first_open = cond.set_index("fish").first_open_s[f]
    pre = [x for x in EP[f]["closed"] if x["seg"][1] <= first_open]
    tot = sum(x["seg"][1] - x["seg"][0] for x in pre)
    r["closed_before_first_open_frac"] = sum(b - a for x in pre for a, b in x["pauses"]) / tot if tot else np.nan
    r["closed_before_first_open_s"] = tot
    rows.append(r)
frac = pd.DataFrame(rows)
print(frac.round(3).to_string(index=False))
w = stats.wilcoxon(frac.open_passive_frac, frac.closed_passive_frac, alternative="greater")
print(f"\nOpen loop: median {frac.open_passive_frac.median():.3f}; closed loop: median {frac.closed_passive_frac.median():.3f}; "
      f"open higher in {(frac.open_passive_frac > frac.closed_passive_frac).sum()} of {len(frac)} fish; Wilcoxon p = {w.pvalue:.3g}")
v = frac.dropna(subset=["closed_before_first_open_frac"])
w2 = stats.wilcoxon(v.open_passive_frac, v.closed_before_first_open_frac, alternative="greater")
print(f"Variant, closed loop before the first open loop: median {v.closed_before_first_open_frac.median():.3f}; "
      f"open higher in {(v.open_passive_frac > v.closed_before_first_open_frac).sum()} of {len(v)} fish; Wilcoxon p = {w2.pvalue:.3g}")
# By gain level in closed loop.
rows = []
for s in sessions:
    m = fv.condition_masks(s)
    for g in np.unique(np.round(s["gain"][m["closed"]], 3)):
        mask = m["closed"] & (np.round(s["gain"], 3) == g)
        segs = fv.segments(s["cond_t"], mask)
        tot = sum(b - a for a, b in segs)
        if tot < 60:
            continue
        ep = [fv.epochs_in_segment(s["swims"], seg) for seg in segs]
        rows.append({"fish": s["fish"], "gain": g, "seconds": tot, "passive_frac": sum(b - a for e in ep for a, b in e["pauses"]) / tot})
print("\nClosed-loop passive fraction by gain level (levels with 60 s or more):")
print(pd.DataFrame(rows).round(3).to_string(index=False))

# By gain level, split into closed loop before and after the first open loop, with the protocol
# codes of the blocks (levels with 30 s or more in a part).
rows = []
for s in sessions:
    m = fv.condition_masks(s)
    first_open = cond.set_index("fish").first_open_s[s["fish"]]
    g_r = np.round(s["gain"], 3)
    for part, pm in [("before", s["cond_t"] < first_open), ("after", s["cond_t"] >= first_open)]:
        for g in np.unique(g_r[m["closed"] & pm]):
            mask = m["closed"] & pm & (g_r == g)
            segs = fv.segments(s["cond_t"], mask)
            tot = sum(b - a for a, b in segs)
            if tot < 30:
                continue
            ep = [fv.epochs_in_segment(s["swims"], seg) for seg in segs]
            rows.append({"fish": s["fish"], "part": part, "gain": g, "codes": sorted(set(s["protocol_code"][mask].astype(int))),
                         "seconds": tot, "passive_frac": sum(b - a for e in ep for a, b in e["pauses"]) / tot})
bygain = pd.DataFrame(rows)
print("\nClosed-loop passive fraction by gain level, before and after the first open loop:")
print(bygain.round(3).to_string(index=False))

    d = bygain[bygain.part == part]

          f"passivity lower at the highest gain than at the lowest in {(ends['last'] < ends['first']).sum()}")

Result: not reproduced. Over all closed-loop time the fish spend a median 0.546 of the time in pauses of 5 s or more, against 0.551 in open loop; open loop is higher in 7 of 12 fish (Wilcoxon p = 0.285), and the closed-loop median is far above 10%. Restricted to closed loop before the first open loop (a variant), the median is 0.104 and open loop is higher in 8 of 10 fish (p = 0.0137). By gain level, closed-loop passivity has a median of 0.183 before the first open loop and 0.825 after it. Passivity shows no consistent fall with the gain: it is lower at the highest gain than at the lowest in 2 of 7 fish before the first open loop and 3 of 7 after it, though before the first open loop 2 fish are tied at 0.000 and one differs by 0.006. The gain is in arbitrary units and no level can be identified as the paper's naturalistic gain.

The outcome rests on the choice of closed-loop time. The closed-loop blocks after the first open loop, where passivity is high, decide it. The variant restricted to closed loop before the first open loop is closer to the paper's comparison and meets the criterion for partially reproduced (test passes, median 0.104 above 10%). The main reading was fixed before the analysis and is kept.

fig1c-vigor-open-loop-onset¶

When switched from closed to open loop, fish first swim with higher vigor, then stop swimming.

Criterion: per switch, mean power of the bouts from the switch to the first passive epoch over the mean power of the closed-loop bouts in the 30 s before; per fish the median log ratio; one-sided Wilcoxon over fish. Switches with fewer than 3 bouts on either side are left out.

In [14]:
def switch_ratios(s, strict=False):
    m = fv.condition_masks(s)
    t = s["cond_t"]
    sw = s["swims"].sort_values("start_time")
    out = []
    switches = t[1:][m["closed"][:-1] & m["open"][1:]]
    for t0 in switches:
        before = sw[(sw.start_time >= t0 - 30) & (sw.stop_time <= t0)]
        before = before[fv.label_at(s, before.start_time.to_numpy()) == 1]
        if strict and not m["closed"][(t >= t0 - 30) & (t < t0)].all():
            continue
        t_end = t[np.flatnonzero((t > t0) & ~m["open"])[0]] if ((t > t0) & ~m["open"]).any() else t[-1]
        after = sw[(sw.start_time >= t0) & (sw.start_time < t_end)]
        st, sp = after.start_time.to_numpy(), after.stop_time.to_numpy()
        if len(st) == 0 or st[0] - t0 >= fv.PASSIVE_GAP_S:
            out.append({"t": t0, "n_before": len(before), "n_after": 0, "log_ratio": np.nan})
            continue
        g = np.flatnonzero(st[1:] - sp[:-1] >= fv.PASSIVE_GAP_S)
        after = after.iloc[:(g[0] + 1) if len(g) else len(st)]
        after = after[fv.label_at(s, after.start_time.to_numpy()) == 2]
        ok = len(before) >= 3 and len(after) >= 3 and before.power.mean() > 0
        out.append({"t": t0, "n_before": len(before), "n_after": len(after),
                    "log_ratio": np.log(after.power.mean() / before.power.mean()) if ok else np.nan})
    return pd.DataFrame(out)

# Synthetic check: closed loop 0 to 60 s, open loop 60 to 70 s, then closed loop. Bouts every 2 s
# before the switch (power 1), every 1 s in the open loop (power 3), and every 1 s afterwards
# (power 100) with no pause of 5 s. Only the open-loop bouts may count: the ratio must be 3.
syn_t = np.arange(0, 200, 0.1)
syn = {"cond_t": syn_t, "gain": np.where((syn_t >= 60) & (syn_t < 70), 0.0, 0.02), "velocity": np.ones_like(syn_t),
       "swims": pd.DataFrame({"start_time": np.r_[np.arange(30, 60, 2.0), np.arange(60.5, 70, 1.0), np.arange(70.5, 150, 1.0)]})}
syn["swims"]["stop_time"] = syn["swims"].start_time + 0.2
syn["swims"]["power"] = np.where(syn["swims"].start_time < 60, 1.0, np.where(syn["swims"].start_time < 70, 3.0, 100.0))
print("synthetic switch, power ratio:", np.round(np.exp(switch_ratios(syn).log_ratio.to_numpy()), 3))

rows = []
for s in sessions:
    r = switch_ratios(s)
    rs = switch_ratios(s, strict=True)
    rows.append({"fish": s["fish"], "switches": len(r), "used": int(r.log_ratio.notna().sum()) if len(r) else 0,
                 "median_log_ratio": r.log_ratio.median() if len(r) else np.nan,
                 "strict_used": int(rs.log_ratio.notna().sum()) if len(rs) else 0,
                 "strict_median_log_ratio": rs.log_ratio.median() if len(rs) else np.nan})
vig = pd.DataFrame(rows)
vig["median_ratio"] = np.exp(vig.median_log_ratio)
print(vig.round(3).to_string(index=False))
d = vig.median_log_ratio.dropna()
w = stats.wilcoxon(d, alternative="greater")
print(f"\n{len(d)} fish with a usable switch; ratio above 1 in {(d > 0).sum()}; median ratio {np.exp(d.median()):.2f} "
      f"(range {np.exp(d.min()):.2f} to {np.exp(d.max()):.2f}); Wilcoxon p = {w.pvalue:.3g}")
ds = vig.strict_median_log_ratio.dropna()
if len(ds) > 1:
    print(f"Variant requiring 30 s of closed loop before the switch: {len(ds)} fish, ratio above 1 in {(ds > 0).sum()}, "
          f"median ratio {np.exp(ds.median()):.2f}, Wilcoxon p = {stats.wilcoxon(ds, alternative='greater').pvalue:.3g}")

fig1i-isi-before-passivity¶

Before the switch to passivity the inter-swim interval increases progressively, and fish swim more vigorously and less frequently in the seconds before passivity.

Criterion: in active epochs of 10 or more bouts that end in passivity (open loop), intervals k = 1 (last) to 7 back and bout powers; interval at k = 1 longer than at k = 7 (one-sided Wilcoxon over fish), negative Spearman correlation of k with the group mean, and the last 3 bouts more powerful than bouts 8 to 10 back (one-sided Wilcoxon).

In [15]:
def before_passivity(min_bouts, epochs=EP):
    rows = []
    for s in sessions:
        isis, pws = [], []
        for x in epochs[s["fish"]]["open"]:
            for e in x["active"]:
                if e["followed_by_passive"] and e["n_bouts"] >= min_bouts:
                    isis.append(np.diff(e["bout_starts"])[::-1][:7])
                    pw = e["bout_powers"][::-1][:10]
                    pws.append(np.r_[pw, np.full(10 - len(pw), np.nan)])
        if isis:
            I, P = np.mean(isis, 0), np.nanmean(pws, 0)
            rows.append({"fish": s["fish"], "epochs": len(isis), **{f"isi_k{k + 1}": I[k] for k in range(7)},
                         "power_last3": P[:3].mean(), "power_8to10": P[7:10].mean()})
    return pd.DataFrame(rows)

def judge(df, label):
    w_isi = stats.wilcoxon(df.isi_k1, df.isi_k7, alternative="greater")
    means = df[[f"isi_k{k}" for k in range(1, 8)]].mean()
    rho = stats.spearmanr(np.arange(1, 8), means.to_numpy())
    w_pow = stats.wilcoxon(df.power_last3, df.power_8to10, alternative="greater", nan_policy="omit")
    print(f"{label}: {len(df)} fish; mean interval k=1 {df.isi_k1.mean():.3f} s, k=7 {df.isi_k7.mean():.3f} s, "
          f"k=1 longer in {(df.isi_k1 > df.isi_k7).sum()} fish, Wilcoxon p = {w_isi.pvalue:.3g}; "
          f"Spearman rho (k, mean) = {rho.statistic:.3f}; power last 3 {df.power_last3.mean():.3f} against bouts 8-10 back "
          f"{df.power_8to10.mean():.3f}, higher in {(df.power_last3 > df.power_8to10).sum()} fish, Wilcoxon p = {w_pow.pvalue:.3g}")
    return means

bp = before_passivity(10)
print(bp.round(3).to_string(index=False))
print()
means = judge(bp, "Main (10 or more bouts)")
print("Mean interval by k (1 = last):", means.round(3).to_dict())
judge(before_passivity(8), "Variant (8 or more bouts)")
judge(before_passivity(15), "Variant (15 or more bouts)")
_ = judge(before_passivity(10, EPX), "Variant (10 or more bouts, edge epochs kept)")

Variant (15 or more bouts): 10 fish; mean interval k=1 1.534 s, k=7 1.116 s, k=1 longer in 9 fish, Wilcoxon p = 0.00195; Spearman rho (k, mean) = -0.607; power last 3 0.429 against bouts 8-10 back 0.406, higher in 4 fish, Wilcoxon p = 0.423
Variant (10 or more bouts, edge epochs kept): 11 fish; mean interval k=1 1.468 s, k=7 1.322 s, k=1 longer in 8 fish, Wilcoxon p = 0.0874; Spearman rho (k, mean) = -0.357; power last 3 0.643 against bouts 8-10 back 0.574, higher in 6 fish, Wilcoxon p = 0.139

Result: not reproduced. In active epochs of 10 or more bouts that end in passivity (11 fish), the last interval (1.506 s) is longer than the seventh from last (1.312 s) in 8 fish, but not significantly (Wilcoxon p = 0.103). The Spearman rho of k against the mean interval is -0.536, but only k = 1 stands out: the means for k = 2 to 7 lie between 1.274 and 1.357 s with no trend. The last 3 bouts are not more powerful than bouts 8 to 10 back (0.636 against 0.575, higher in 6 fish, p = 0.16). The outcome depends on the minimum epoch length, which the paper does not state: with epochs of 8 or more bouts both parts hold (intervals p = 0.00806, rho = -0.286; power p = 0.0269), and with 15 or more the interval part holds (p = 0.00195) and the power part does not (p = 0.423). Keeping the epochs cut by either edge of an open-loop period (a variant) gives p = 0.0874 for the intervals and p = 0.139 for the power.

Signals around passivity onset¶

The whole-brain signal of each cell type around each passivity onset, against the baseline 10 to 5 s before onset (in the units of the stored series; see the data check).

LAGS = np.arange(-15, 20.01, 0.5)
TRACES, rows = {}, []
for s in sessions:
    for name in s["imaging"]:
        f = s["fish"]
        t = s["imaging"][name]["t"]
        y = WB[(f, name, 0.0)][0].astype(float)
        ok = ~fv.censored(y)
        t, y = t[ok], y[ok]
        on = ON[f]
        base = fv.window_mean(t, y, on, fv.BASELINE)
        E = fv.event_windows(t, y, on, LAGS) - base[:, None]
        TRACES[(f, name)] = (t, y, on, base, E)
        rows.append({"fish": f, "series": name, "onsets": len(on), "trace_sd": y.std()})
print(pd.DataFrame(rows).round(5).to_string(index=False))

fig, axes = plt.subplots(1, 2, figsize=(11, 3.5))
for ax, name in zip(axes, ["NeuronDfOverF", "GliaDfOverF"]):
    for (f, n), (t, y, on, base, E) in TRACES.items():
        if n == name:
            avg = np.nanmean(E, 0) / y.std()
            ax.plot(LAGS, avg, label=f)
            print(f"{name} {f}: onset-triggered mean in SD units ranges {np.nanmin(avg):.2f} to {np.nanmax(avg):.2f}")
    ax.axvline(0, color="k", lw=0.5); ax.axhline(0, color="k", lw=0.5)
    ax.set_xlabel("time from passivity onset (s)"); ax.set_ylabel("change from baseline (SD of trace)")
    ax.set_title(name.replace("DfOverF", "") + " whole-brain signal"); ax.legend(fontsize=7)
plt.tight_layout(); plt.show()

fig2bc-neurons-lower-in-passivity¶

Whole-brain average neuronal activity is higher during active behavior than during passivity, and decays after passivity onset.

Criterion: per fish, mean neuronal signal over open-loop passive epochs minus that over open-loop active epochs; below 0 by a one-sided Wilcoxon over the 8 fish.

In [17]:
rows = []
for s in sessions:
    if "NeuronDfOverF" not in s["imaging"]:
        continue
    f = s["fish"]
    t, y, on, base, E = TRACES[(f, "NeuronDfOverF")]
    pas = [p for x in EP[f]["open"] for p in x["passive"]]
    act = [(e["start"], e["stop"]) for x in EP[f]["open"] for e in x["active"]]
    diff = fv.mean_in_intervals(t, y, pas) - fv.mean_in_intervals(t, y, act)
    late = fv.window_mean(t, y, on, (5, 10)) - base
    good = np.isfinite(late)
    rows.append({"fish": f, "passive_minus_active": diff, "in_trace_sd": diff / y.std(), "onsets": int(good.sum()),

fig2c-glia-rise-at-passivity¶

Whole-brain average radial astrocyte calcium increases before passivity onset and peaks soon after it.

Criterion: per fish, 1 to 4 s after onset and 2 to 0 s before onset, each against 10 to 5 s before (one-tailed Wilcoxon over onsets), and the peak of the triggered average between 0 and 10 s; reproduced when all hold in at least 3 of 4 fish, partially when the after-onset increase holds in at least 3.

In [18]:
def onset_tests(f, name, onsets=None):
    t, y, on, base, E = TRACES[(f, name)]
    if onsets is not None:
        on = onsets
        base = fv.window_mean(t, y, on, fv.BASELINE)
        E = fv.event_windows(t, y, on, LAGS) - base[:, None]
    resp = fv.window_mean(t, y, on, fv.RESPONSE) - base
    pre = fv.window_mean(t, y, on, (-2, 0)) - base
    good = np.isfinite(resp) & np.isfinite(pre)
    avg = np.nanmean(E, 0)
    return {"fish": f, "onsets": int(good.sum()), "after_1to4": np.median(resp[good]) / y.std(),
            "p_after": stats.wilcoxon(resp[good], alternative="greater").pvalue,
            "before_2to0": np.median(pre[good]) / y.std(),
            "p_before": stats.wilcoxon(pre[good], alternative="greater").pvalue,
            "peak_lag_s": LAGS[np.nanargmax(avg)]}

glia = pd.DataFrame([onset_tests(s["fish"], "GliaDfOverF") for s in sessions if "GliaDfOverF" in s["imaging"]])
glia["after_ok"] = glia.p_after < 0.05
glia["all_ok"] = glia.after_ok & (glia.p_before < 0.05) & glia.peak_lag_s.between(0, 10)
print("Medians in SD units of each fish's trace:")
print(glia.to_string(index=False, float_format=lambda v: f"{v:.3g}"))
print(f"\nAfter-onset increase in {glia.after_ok.sum()} of 4 fish; all three parts in {glia.all_ok.sum()} of 4 fish")
print("Onsets per fish:", glia.set_index("fish").onsets.to_dict(), "(paper's example fish: 64 events)")

Result: not reproduced. The whole-brain glial signal rises before passivity onset and peaks after it in 2 of the 4 two-colour fish (20170228-3 and 20170228-4: 1 to 4 s after onset 0.61 and 0.53 SD above baseline, p = 8.0e-13 and 1.1e-14; 2 to 0 s before, p = 1.7e-11 and 3.6e-17; peaks 3.5 and 2.5 s after onset). In the other two it falls after onset (-0.91 and -0.64 SD, p = 1 for an increase). The criterion needed 3 of 4. One of the matching fish has 67 onsets, close to the 64 events of the paper's example fish. All 26 onsets of 20161109-2 fall in code 32, prolonged open loop with the grating moving, and 42 of the 46 onsets of 20170203-1, so the short alternating blocks do not explain the fall in these two fish.

The split does not depend on the onsets the main rule leaves out: with the edge epochs kept, 1 or 2 onsets are added per fish and the same 2 fish pass. Over the first five onsets after the start of each open-loop period, the glial response 1 to 4 s after onset is again negative in 20161109-2 and 20170203-1 (-1.13 and -0.62 SD) and positive in the other two (0.83 and 1.36 SD). In 20161109-2 and 20170203-1 the glial trace has an SD of 0.0016 and 0.0011, against 0.0097 and 0.0072, and it correlates with the neuronal trace at 0.58 and 0.59, against 0.06 and 0.15 in the other two fish. In 20170203-1 the neuronal trace also has a low SD (0.0016, against 0.0069 to 0.0180 in the other fish) and, unlike the other three two-colour fish, rises after onset (+0.28 SD, p = 0.0023), so the low SD there affects both channels and does not point to the glial channel alone. The data here do not show why these two files differ.

figs2a-open-loop-higher¶

Whole-brain average neuronal and glial calcium are higher and fluctuate more strongly in open loop than in closed loop.

Criterion: per fish, mean and SD of the whole-brain signal in open and closed loop, leaving out 30 s after each switch; neurons by one-sided Wilcoxon over 8 fish, glia in all 4 fish.

In [19]:
rows = []
for (f, name), (t, y, on, base, E) in TRACES.items():
    s = S[f]
    lab = fv.label_at(s, t)
    keep = fv.seconds_since_switch(s, t) >= 30
    r = {"fish": f, "series": name}
    for c, code_ in [("closed", 1), ("open", 2)]:
        sel = keep & (lab == code_)
        r[f"{c}_frames"] = int(sel.sum())
        r[f"{c}_mean"] = (y[sel].mean() - y.mean()) / y.std()
        r[f"{c}_sd"] = y[sel].std() / y.std()
    rows.append(r)
s2a = pd.DataFrame(rows)
s2a["mean_higher_open"] = s2a.open_mean > s2a.closed_mean
s2a["sd_higher_open"] = s2a.open_sd > s2a.closed_sd
print("Means and SDs in units of each fish's whole-trace SD:")
print(s2a.round(3).to_string(index=False))
for name in ["NeuronDfOverF", "GliaDfOverF"]:
    d = s2a[s2a.series == name]
    d = d.dropna(subset=["closed_mean"])
    pm = stats.wilcoxon(d.open_mean, d.closed_mean, alternative="greater").pvalue
    ps = stats.wilcoxon(d.open_sd, d.closed_sd, alternative="greater").pvalue
    print(f"{name}: mean higher in open loop in {d.mean_higher_open.sum()} of {len(d)} fish (Wilcoxon p = {pm:.3g}, "
          f"median difference {np.median(d.open_mean - d.closed_mean):.2f} SD); SD higher in {d.sd_higher_open.sum()} of {len(d)} "
          f"(p = {ps:.3g}, median ratio {np.median(d.open_sd / d.closed_sd):.2f})")

# Variant for the SD: computed within each continuous closed- or open-loop period (after the first
# 30 s), raw or after removing a linear trend, then averaged over periods weighted by frames.
rows = []
for (f, name), (t, y, on, base, E) in TRACES.items():
    s = S[f]
    lab = fv.label_at(s, t)
    keep = fv.seconds_since_switch(s, t) >= 30
    r = {"fish": f, "series": name}
    for c, code_ in [("closed", 1), ("open", 2)]:
        sel = keep & (lab == code_)
        runs = np.split(np.flatnonzero(sel), np.flatnonzero(np.diff(np.flatnonzero(sel)) > 1) + 1)
        runs = [i for i in runs if len(i) >= 10]
        n = np.array([len(i) for i in runs])
        sd_raw = np.array([y[i].std() for i in runs]) / y.std()
        sd_det = np.array([(y[i] - np.polyval(np.polyfit(t[i], y[i], 1), t[i])).std() for i in runs]) / y.std()
        r[f"{c}_periods"] = len(runs)
        r[f"{c}_sd_within"] = np.average(sd_raw, weights=n) if len(runs) else np.nan
        r[f"{c}_sd_detrended"] = np.average(sd_det, weights=n) if len(runs) else np.nan
    rows.append(r)
s2v = pd.DataFrame(rows)
print("\nSD within periods (periods of 10 frames or more), in units of each fish's whole-trace SD:")
print(s2v.round(3).to_string(index=False))
for name in ["NeuronDfOverF", "GliaDfOverF"]:
    d = s2v[s2v.series == name].dropna()
    for k in ["sd_within", "sd_detrended"]:
        p = stats.wilcoxon(d[f"open_{k}"], d[f"closed_{k}"], alternative="greater").pvalue
        print(f"{name} {k}: higher in open loop in {(d[f'open_{k}'] > d[f'closed_{k}']).sum()} of {len(d)} fish "
              f"(Wilcoxon p = {p:.3g}, median ratio {np.median(d[f'open_{k}'] / d[f'closed_{k}']):.2f})")

# Variant for the SD: windows of equal length (10 s, after the first 30 s of each period), the SD
# within each window, averaged with equal weight over the windows of each condition. This compares
# the same time scale in both conditions, whatever the length of the periods.
WIN_S = 10.0
rows = []
for (f, name), (t, y, on, base, E) in TRACES.items():
    s = S[f]
    lab = fv.label_at(s, t)
    keep = fv.seconds_since_switch(s, t) >= 30
    n_win = int(round(WIN_S / np.median(np.diff(t))))
    r = {"fish": f, "series": name, "frames_per_window": n_win}
    for c, code_ in [("closed", 1), ("open", 2)]:
        sel = keep & (lab == code_)
        runs = np.split(np.flatnonzero(sel), np.flatnonzero(np.diff(np.flatnonzero(sel)) > 1) + 1)
        sds = [y[i[k:k + n_win]].std() / y.std() for i in runs for k in range(0, len(i) - n_win + 1, n_win)]
        r[f"{c}_windows"] = len(sds)
        r[f"{c}_sd_10s"] = np.mean(sds) if sds else np.nan
    rows.append(r)
s2w = pd.DataFrame(rows)
print("\nSD within 10 s windows, in units of each fish's whole-trace SD:")
print(s2w.round(3).to_string(index=False))
for name in ["NeuronDfOverF", "GliaDfOverF"]:
    d = s2w[s2w.series == name].dropna()
    p = stats.wilcoxon(d.open_sd_10s, d.closed_sd_10s, alternative="greater").pvalue
    print(f"{name} SD in 10 s windows: higher in open loop in {(d.open_sd_10s > d.closed_sd_10s).sum()} of {len(d)} fish "
          f"(Wilcoxon p = {p:.3g}, median ratio {np.median(d.open_sd_10s / d.closed_sd_10s):.2f})")

Result: partially reproduced. For neurons, the whole-brain signal is higher in open than closed loop in 6 of 8 fish (Wilcoxon p = 0.0195) and fluctuates more in 7 of 8 (p = 0.0078, median SD ratio 2.98). For glia, both hold in 3 of the 4 fish, not in all 4 as the criterion required; 20170203-1 is the exception. With the SD taken within each continuous period, raw or after removing a linear trend (a variant), it is higher in open loop in 8 of 8 neuron fish (p = 0.0039, median ratios 3.72 and 5.15) and in 4 of 4 glia fish (median ratios 5.04 and 6.11). These periods differ in length (in 20170228-3, 10 closed-loop periods over 213 frames against 2 open-loop periods over 5477), and a long period holds slow fluctuations that a short one cannot. With the SD taken in windows of 10 s in both conditions (a variant), it is higher in open loop in 7 of 8 neuron fish (p = 0.0195, median ratio 2.52) and 3 of 4 glia fish (median ratio 2.07), with 20170203-1 again the exception, where the closed loop gives 12 windows.

fig2h-glia-weaker-closed-loop-pauses¶

When fish in closed loop stop swimming because the stimulus stops moving, glial calcium signals are weaker than during futility-induced passivity.

Criterion: closed-loop pauses (5 s or more, starting while the gain is above 0) against open-loop passivity onsets, response 1 to 4 s after minus 10 to 5 s before; one-sided Mann-Whitney per fish with 3 or more pauses.

In [20]:
rows = []
for s in sessions:
    if "GliaDfOverF" not in s["imaging"]:
        continue
    f = s["fish"]
    t, y, on, base, E = TRACES[(f, "GliaDfOverF")]
    r_open = fv.window_mean(t, y, on, fv.RESPONSE) - base
    cp = fv.closed_loop_pause_onsets(s)
    r_cl = fv.window_mean(t, y, cp, fv.RESPONSE) - fv.window_mean(t, y, cp, fv.BASELINE)
    r_open, r_cl = r_open[np.isfinite(r_open)], r_cl[np.isfinite(r_cl)]
    stationary = np.mean(s["velocity"][np.clip(np.searchsorted(s["cond_t"], cp), 0, len(s["cond_t"]) - 1)] == 0) if len(cp) else np.nan
    rows.append({"fish": f, "closed_pauses": len(r_cl), "share_in_stationary": stationary, "open_onsets": len(r_open),
                 "closed_median": np.median(r_cl) / y.std() if len(r_cl) else np.nan, "open_median": np.median(r_open) / y.std(),
                 "p": stats.mannwhitneyu(r_cl, r_open, alternative="less").pvalue if len(r_cl) >= 3 else np.nan})
h = pd.DataFrame(rows)
h["smaller_median"] = h.closed_median < h.open_median
print("Medians in units of each fish's trace SD:")
print(h.to_string(index=False, float_format=lambda v: f"{v:.3g}"))
kept = h[h.closed_pauses >= 3]
print(f"\n{len(kept)} fish with 3 or more closed-loop pauses; pause response smaller with p < 0.05 in {(kept.p < 0.05).sum()}, "
      f"smaller in median in {kept.smaller_median.sum()}")

# Variants: (1) the gain above 0 over the whole window, 10 s before to 4 s after the pause onset;
# (2) open-loop onsets with the edge epochs kept; (3) both.
rows = []
for s in sessions:
    if "GliaDfOverF" not in s["imaging"]:
        continue
    f = s["fish"]
    t, y = TRACES[(f, "GliaDfOverF")][:2]
    for label, whole, onsets in [("whole window", True, ON[f]), ("edge epochs kept", False, ONX[f]), ("both", True, ONX[f])]:
        r_open = fv.window_mean(t, y, onsets, fv.RESPONSE) - fv.window_mean(t, y, onsets, fv.BASELINE)
        cp = fv.closed_loop_pause_onsets(s, whole_window=whole)
        r_cl = fv.window_mean(t, y, cp, fv.RESPONSE) - fv.window_mean(t, y, cp, fv.BASELINE)
        r_open, r_cl = r_open[np.isfinite(r_open)], r_cl[np.isfinite(r_cl)]
        rows.append({"variant": label, "fish": f, "closed_pauses": len(r_cl), "open_onsets": len(r_open),
                     "closed_median": np.median(r_cl) / y.std() if len(r_cl) else np.nan, "open_median": np.median(r_open) / y.std(),
                     "p": stats.mannwhitneyu(r_cl, r_open, alternative="less").pvalue if len(r_cl) >= 3 else np.nan})
hv = pd.DataFrame(rows)
print(hv.to_string(index=False, float_format=lambda v: f"{v:.3g}"))
for label, d in hv.groupby("variant", sort=False):
    d = d[d.closed_pauses >= 3]
    print(f"{label}: {len(d)} fish with 3 or more pauses; smaller with p < 0.05 in {(d.p < 0.05).sum()}, smaller in median in {(d.closed_median < d.open_median).sum()}")

Result: not reproduced. The glial response to closed-loop pauses is smaller than to open-loop passivity onsets in 2 of 4 fish (20170228-3 and 20170228-4, Mann-Whitney p = 1.1e-05 and 5.0e-11), the two fish whose glia rise at passivity. In the other two, glia fall after passivity onset, and the pause response is not smaller (p = 0.78 and 0.98). Requiring the gain above 0 over the whole window from 10 s before to 4 s after the pause, keeping the edge epochs, or both (variants) give the same 2 of 4.

Summary¶

A failure to reproduce here may be a failure of this attempt, not of the paper: see the reasoning and the differences from the paper's method.

How the analysis differs from the paper's.

  • The behavioural claims use the 12 imaged fish; the paper's behavioural numbers come from 74 (61 for Figure 1I). The Methods' epoch rule is applied to the dandiset's swim bouts, with pauses measured from the end of one bout to the start of the next; the dandiset's own state table is shown as a variant. Epochs cut by the edges of a condition period are left out, which drops the first passivity onset of some open-loop periods (0 to 8 per fish); a variant keeps them for fig1h, fig1i, fig2c and fig2h and changes none of these outcomes. It was not run for methods-isi, fig1j or fig2bc.
  • Closed and open loop are read from the gain signal, and stationary-grating time is left out; the protocol codes in the files have no description.
  • The cell traces are used as stored. They are not ΔF/F as the Methods define it, and the two groups of files were processed differently, so every imaging comparison is made within a fish and scaled by the SD of that fish's trace.
  • The whole-brain signal is the mean over about 8 to 15% of ROIs (8 evenly spaced blocks); two disjoint subsets agree (correlation 0.981 and 0.998).
  • The paper's glial claims rest on NMF components clustered across fish and registered to a template, mostly in a lateral hindbrain region (L-MO); here only the whole-brain average is tested, as the paper shows for its two-colour example fish (Figure 2C).
  • Glia were tested in the 4 two-colour fish, whose glia carry jRGECO1b; the paper's NMF analysis used 6 fish with glial GCaMP6f, of which the dandiset holds 3 without processed traces.

What was found about the dandiset.

  • It holds the 12 imaging sessions of the paper's Figure 2 and related panels, with behaviour, but none of the perturbation or NE imaging experiments of Figures 4 to 6. Undescribed protocols (randomised gain, brief grating speed-ups) may belong to Figures 1K and 7 but cannot be identified.
  • Four files have raw images only; three of them are the only glia-only GCaMP6f recordings.
  • The glial plane of the two-colour files is labelled GCaMP6f but excited at 561 nm and detected at 660 nm (jRGECO1b). The raw images are typed TwoPhotonSeries from a light-sheet microscope.
  • The DfOverF series are not ΔF/F (mean-normalised in 4 files, zero-centred and partly censored in the other 4), and the Fluorescence series look like baselines, with the same description.
  • Imaging is missing for part of three sessions (20170113-2: 2135 of 9751 triggered volumes; raw images of 20170113-4 and 20170228-4).
  • The ActivityStates table is undocumented, does not follow the Methods' definition (active rows of 5 s or less, transient rows duplicating active rows) and has 3 rows in the glia-only files.
  • The protocol codes, gain and velocity signals carry no units or descriptions. Code 33 is a 0.3 to 0.5 s speed-up of the grating in open loop, code 52 a randomised gain, and codes 51 and 53 do not consistently mark closed and open loop.
  • TotalStimulusVelocitySignal, described as the drift speed minus the gain times swim power, stays between -0.002 and 0.008, so the visual feedback of each bout is not recorded.
  • In two of the four two-colour files (20161109-2, 20170203-1) the glial whole-brain trace has a SD of 0.0016 and 0.0011 (0.0097 and 0.0072 in the others) and correlates 0.58 and 0.59 with the neuronal trace (0.06 and 0.15 in the others). In 20170203-1 the neuronal trace also has a low SD (0.0016).
